title: Windows audit entegrasyon testlerindeki CI hatasını gider
name: windows-audit-suite
description: Önce güncel development CI sonucunda Windows matrix integration işindeki test/integration/audit.test.ts hatasının sürüp sürmediğini doğrula. accept-shell-h3a3 node’u Windows kabul komutlarında POSIX shell ve tek tırnak sorununu zaten giderdi; bu düzeltmeyi ve mevcut testleri dikkate al. Sorun sürüyorsa başarısız testi yeniden üret, platforma bağlı yol/shell/git/zamanlama nedenini audit kodu ve testini birlikte düzelterek gider; geçtiyse kanıtla ve gereksiz kod değişikliği yapma. Ayrı ubuntu-latest pnpm audit işini Windows audit testiyle karıştırma.

brief.approach:
**Status, checked 2026-09-24.** The failure still happens. Every CI run on the recent PR branches (for example run 36011978968, `sober/thinking-verbs-8er2`) fails `integration (windows-latest)`. The same failures reproduce on this Windows machine. `pnpm vitest run --project integration test/integration/audit.test.ts test/integration/scan.test.ts` gives 10 failed / 12 passed: 9 in `audit.test.ts` and 1 in `scan.test.ts`. The job has a third failure, in `review.test.ts`.

**Root cause: test fixtures, not production code.** accept-shell-h3a3 made acceptance commands, `dispatch.verify` and `scan.extra` run through `posixShell()` (`packages/core/src/audit.ts`, used by `packages/core/src/scan.ts:211`). That is correct: those commands are POSIX shell by contract. The test fixtures still build commands like `` `${process.execPath} -e "process.exit(0)"` ``. On Windows, `process.execPath` is `C:\hostedtoolcache\...\node.exe`. `sh` reads each unquoted backslash as an escape, so the path turns into `C:hostedtoolcache...`, and the command is not found. The run then exits 127, which the code reads as `did-not-run`. So each criterion's result is `null` or `did-not-run`, never the exit the test expects.

**Fix.**
1. Add one export to `test/integration/fixture.ts`. It is the node binary as a POSIX-shell word: forward slashes, double-quoted, so a path with spaces also works.
   `export const NODE_SH = JSON.stringify(process.execPath.replaceAll('\\', '/'))`
   Git for Windows' `sh` resolves `C:/...` paths. On Linux and macOS this is the same path, quoted.
2. `test/integration/audit.test.ts`: replace every `${process.execPath}` that builds a command for the shell with `${NODE_SH}`. That is `exits()`, `missing`, the worktree-marker criterion and the `expected 200, got 401` criterion. Check `FAKE_HOST` (line 29) separately. It is the host command, not an acceptance command. Change it only if it also goes through `posixShell()`; otherwise leave it.
3. `test/integration/scan.test.ts:155`: the `extra` scanner command uses `${NODE_SH}` in the same way.
4. `test/integration/review.test.ts:356`, "a record that cannot be written after the merge takes the merge back". The test uses `chmodSync(dir, 0o555)` to make the nodes directory unwritable. Windows ignores POSIX mode bits on directories, so the write succeeds and the merge stands. Add `|| process.platform === 'win32'` to the existing `test.skipIf`, and extend the comment above it: a directory's mode bits do not stop a write on Windows either. Do not try to emulate read-only with ACLs. The other two platforms keep the coverage.

**Out of scope.**
- No change to `packages/core/src/audit.ts`, `git.ts` or `scan.ts`: the shell behaviour is the contract.
- No change to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- The separate `ubuntu-latest` `pnpm audit` job is a different thing and is not touched.
- The flaky core unit tests (`packages/core/src/sync.test.ts` EBUSY/timeouts, `models.test.ts` executable check, `agent.test.ts` EPERM) are not part of this node.
- The other 15 integration files that use `process.execPath` stay as they are unless they fail. Most spawn `node` directly, with no shell.

acceptance.run: pnpm vitest run --project integration test/integration/audit.test.ts test/integration/scan.test.ts test/integration/review.test.ts
acceptance.proves: the three integration files that fail in the Windows CI job pass on this Windows machine
no shell command in those fixtures is still built from the raw, backslashed node path
production code and CI config are untouched: the fix is in the tests, where the cause is
